posts.hook: A $14 chip, a hidden mic, and an arrest inside OpenAI
posts.caption: an openai engineer is arrested over a hidden recording device in an executive room, anthropic builds its own replacement for git, microsoft ships a record batch of security fixes. full digest at sift.yasint.dev (link in bio)

slides.title: An OpenAI engineer is charged over a hidden recording device in an executive room
slides.desc: A filing says it was a ==$14== dev board sold online. Leaking executive talks takes little hardware.

slides.title: Anthropic built its own alternative to Git
slides.desc: Merged changes went from about 2,500 a day in May to over ==30,000== by September.

slides.title: Microsoft patched more than 1,400 flaws in one batch, a record
slides.desc: September's record was nearly 1,000. One flaw was already exploited in the wild.

slides.title: OpenAI is in early talks to buy security firm Trail of Bits
slides.desc: A 40-person firm that finds and fixes open-source vulnerabilities, part of OpenAI's cyber push.

slides.title: The FBI shut down 40+ laptop farms used to place North Koreans in US tech jobs
slides.desc: The scheme used stolen identities to get hired remotely, aimed at hiring rather than networks.

slides.title: Linus Torvalds experiments with AI-generated kernel code
slides.desc: Linuxiac reports a 3x speedup, a signal from a project with a strict review culture.
